newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada office space among world's cheapest - survey.
newsitem.headline: Canada office space among world's cheapest - survey.

text.p: Canadian office space is among the most affordable in the world, although growing demand is sending rents higher, according to a Royal LePage -sponsored study released on Monday.
The survey of worldwide occupancy costs found Calgary had the lowest office rents of any major city in the world in 1997 after Houston.
The study estimated the cost of available office space was US$16.70 a square foot in Calgary, or C$23.19, compared with US$14.85 in Houston.

Office rents in Toronto, Montreal and Vancouver were also considered low by world standards. Montreal had the second lowest average rents of surveyed Canadian cities at C$23.47 a square foot, followed by Toronto at C$26.67 and Vancouver at C$34.25.
By contrast, available office space in Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London cost more than US$90 a square foot.

But while Canadian office space was cheaper, rents were rising. From 1996 to 1997, rents for available office space rose in Calgary, Vancouver and Montreal. An expanding economy, increasing demand and the lack of new construction were helping increase rents in most cities, analysts said.

"It's quite likely that Canadian costs are going to rise, probably faster over the next little while than international costs, but still will be comparatively a good deal," said Royal LePage vice-president Brad Henderson.
